newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria oilworkers' union threatens to stike.
newsitem.headline: Algeria oilworkers' union threatens to stike.

text.p: Algeria's 38,000-strong oil and gas workers' union has threatened to strike to back claims for a wage raise, Algerian newspapers said on Tuesday.
Workers at the state-owned gas and oil giant Sonatrach accused the company directorate for backtracking on a pay increase agreement reached last week, Algerian newspapers reported.
Union officials, speaking by telephone from Algiers, said the union would lodge later on Tuesday a month's warning of strike action but refused to give more details about their threat.

They said the directorate agreed last week to increase wages by 15 percent backdated to last January before saying the hike will be given in installments starting next January and only to employees in the lower pay scales.

Liberte newspaper said on Tuesday the union believed the energy ministry had forced Sonatrach directorate to amend the agreement. There was no immediate comments from the ministry or Sonatrach officials.
The oil and gas union has threatened several times in the past two years to strike to pressure the government, before withdrawing the threat at the last minute.
